items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Brunis and Jack and myself, and we'd run in together.

ctx.x: but he was drunk all the time, you know. And so, you'd go ask him something about a horn. Get away from here, kid, can't you see I'm busy. He had chicks and all, but that's why I can never turn a kid down today because I think of those things. And actually, the guy probably know too much to tell me anyway because they really didn't know. You know, they hadn't made a scientific study of it. They really just didn't know. He couldn't have -- probably couldn't have told me.

In later years I found out that -- I would look for guys who knew these things and there weren't too many trombone players who know them. Even when I came long with -- Jack Teagarden and myself -- we always used to jam a lot and get together. Brunis and Jack and myself, and we'd run in together. Sit around -- Higginbotham -- we'd jam.

But they didn't -- some of their horns were so dirty. You'd be surprised, man. You'd run water through there -- roaches, anything liable to jump out of that horn, you know. But they didn't know. They didn't know about -- everybody drank a lot. You wasn't making no money. So, you'd try to have some fun.
